title: Data cards and synthetic tables: a table described without its rows, and invented rows with the same traps
request: A training example should be able to carry a table without carrying a person's rows. A data card describes every table that reaches DCLab, and a synthetic table is drawn from the card with the same roles, relations and planted problems.
spec: A dclab_core contract, DataCard: per column its role, dtype and bands, and the aggregates needed to draw it again; the relations between columns and tables; the problems they show. synthesize(card) returns invented tables. Done when, on the fraud replica, the card and a table drawn from it reproduce the roles and the planted traps, and the drawn table shares no row with the source.
plan: Bands in one module (dclab_core.bands) so a card and a decision's state band a column the same way.
Relations measured on the source: key, join, disjoint, agrees, equals, null_when, one_to_one. Problems are derived from them, never from values.
A draw that rebuilds each column from its card, then applies the relations, and copies the label table's matched rows from the invented main table.

decisions.decision: Category names become codes (status_a, status_b) unless the caller keeps them for a public or synthetic table.
decisions.why: A category can be a person's name, a city or a shop.

decisions.decision: Numeric identifiers are drawn above the source's largest value.
decisions.why: A drawn id that equals a source id would point at a real customer or account.

decisions.decision: The traps are found as relations and problems, not declared by the replica.
decisions.why: The same card can then find them in a person's own tables.

change: dclab_core/datacard.py (new; dclab-core 0.12.0), dclab_core/bands.py (new; ledger re-exports it), dclab_core/contracts.py, schemas data_card; dclab_rnd/studio/data.py (data_card, data.card), dclab_rnd/draft/pipeline.py (draft data_card, rebuilt when a label file arrives), agentic/routers/projects.py (attach off the event loop), dclab_rnd/ledger/__init__.py; tests/test_data_card.py (new); CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, the plan, the roadmap.

findings.defect: A numeric id stored as an integer in one file and as a float in the other made one id look like two.
findings.scenario: biker_id 622233 in the sample and 622233.0 in the rides was reported as one name with two meanings.
findings.fix: One normal form for comparing values across tables.

findings.defect: Quantiles rounded to three significant digits flattened coordinates.
findings.scenario: A longitude near 45.0 became constant, and the drawn table lost its spread.
findings.cause: The rounding was relative to the value, not to the spread.
findings.fix: Round to a hundredth of the spread.

findings.defect: A circular import: the card needed the ledger's bands while the ledger was still loading.
findings.cause: contracts imports ledger, which imports contracts.
findings.fix: dclab_core.bands, a module with no dependency, imported by both.

findings.defect: Numeric quantiles kept one person's exact value.
findings.scenario: The highest salary of 200 was stored exactly, as quantile 1.0.
findings.cause: The quantiles included 0 and 1, and the rounding was clamped at units.
findings.fix: Quantiles from the 1st to the 99th percentile (the 5th and 95th under 100 rows), rounded below the units too.

findings.defect: Dates kept the exact first and last day, even for three rows.
findings.scenario: The oldest person's birth date was stored as the start of the range.
findings.cause: min and max, with no row floor.
findings.fix: The 1st and 99th percentile days, only with 20 rows or more.

findings.defect: A numeric level held by one row was kept by name.
findings.scenario: An age of 97, held by one person, was kept with its share.
findings.cause: Numeric levels were kept whenever the column was not named like a key.
findings.fix: Keep the names only when every kept level has 5 rows or more.

findings.defect: One inf in a numeric column lost the whole card.
findings.scenario: The project got no card, silently.
findings.cause: A non-finite quantile failed the contract.
findings.fix: Only finite numbers enter the quantiles.

findings.defect: Drawing a table with a boolean column crashed.
findings.cause: Booleans were treated as numeric levels.

findings.defect: Numeric ids could not be drawn, or were drawn among the source's own ids.
findings.scenario: customer_id 1 to 1000 crashed. account 3 of the replica appeared in the drawn table.
findings.cause: The digit count came from the median, and the draw used the source's range.
findings.fix: Draw above the source's largest value, in a range wide enough, with bounded retries.

findings.defect: Dates and times came back as text.
findings.scenario: Re-carding a drawn table gave dtype string.
findings.fix: Cast to datetime when the card says datetime.

findings.defect: Wide tables blocked the server for a minute and could lose the trap relations.
findings.scenario: 100,000 rows with 25 id columns took 84.5 s inside an async route. Within-table relations filled the cap before the traps.
findings.cause: Text conversion per pair of columns, no cap on pairs, and relations recorded on any coincidence.
findings.fix: One conversion per column, at most 12 id columns compared, equals only from 1% of rows, between-table relations first, the upload off the event loop.

findings.defect: A draft's card ignored a label file that arrived after the table.
findings.scenario: In the usual order the card had no key, coarse join or concentration traps.
findings.cause: The labels branch returned before the card was rebuilt.
findings.fix: Rebuild the card with the label file in that branch.

findings.defect: Long or non-text column names silently cost the card.
findings.scenario: Two 190-character names overflowed a statement. A column named 0 raised a KeyError.
findings.cause: Untruncated names in statements, and keys by str(name) while the frame was indexed by the name itself.
findings.fix: Names shortened in statements, and columns renamed to text first.

findings.defect: Tests did not cover the draft, privacy of numbers and dates, or odd dtypes.
findings.scenario: Exact quantiles and ignored taken ids both passed the suite.
findings.cause: Only the replica path was tested.
findings.fix: Tests for each, and planted faults until each is caught.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each fix undone fails a test
measurements.result: 7 of 13 caught at first; tests sharpened until 11 of 13 caught; the other 2 (a statement cap and a draw-loop guard) are second guards behind another fix

measurements.name: wide table card time
measurements.gate: a card of 100,000 rows and 25 id columns well under the 84.5 s measured
measurements.result: 1.7 s after the fix (5,000 rows and 150 columns: 0.2 s)

outcome: Every table that reaches DCLab gets a card in bands, with no row and no value of one person. A table drawn from the card keeps the roles and the six planted traps of the fraud replica, and shares no row and no identifier with it.
lessons: A quantile at 0 or 1 is one row's value: privacy needs the tails cut, not only rounding.
An invented id must be drawn outside the source's range, or the draw can name a real account.
Test a card with the tables people actually have (booleans, time zones, ids from 1 to n, a column named 0), not only the replica.
risks: A rounded quantile still says roughly where values lie: the scale of a fare, the city of the coordinates.
Relations across rows (a behaviour, a formula between numbers) are not drawn again.
